takeaway: A person moves a copy of the arm, the robot mirrors it, and every moment becomes an example for the robot to imitate.

selfCheck.question: Why steer the robot with a second copy of the arm instead of a joystick?
selfCheck.answer: same shape and joints; each joint moves the matching joint; joystick would need turning stick directions into six joints; partly guessing, joystick never shown.

sentence: A person teaches a robot a task by moving a second copy of the robot's arm by hand. The real robot copies each movement while recording what its camera sees and where its joints are. After enough of these recorded demonstrations, the robot can do the task by itself. The explainer says one 2023 robot needed only about 10 minutes of demonstrations per task.
